To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
B cell clones specific for the hap- ten Ars can be induced to inhibit the IgE response to the Ars hapten by inoculation of an Ars-conjugated protein in CFA.
secondary non-IgG-producing cells of a different specificity are able to suppress the production of IgE antibodies in response to the same antigen.
the synthesis of anti-Ars IgE antibodies is strongly inhibited when secondary B cells specific for the Ars antigen, but of different isotype, are transferred into recipient mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of B cell tolerance to a specific antigen.
the regulation of the IgE response by non-IgE B cells of the same specificity.
the role of regulatory T cells in the induction of IgE responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IgE response to Ars can be inhibited by B cells specific for the same hapten, and this effect does not require the presence of T cells.
the inhibition of an IgE anti-Arshapten response in mice is caused by secondary B cells specific for Ars, but not for the carrier, and that these B cells are of the IgG isotype.
the inhibition is mediated by hapten-specific B cells of the IgG1 subclass, but not of the IgG2a subclass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthesis of antibodies against a hapten is inhibited by the presence in an animal of B cells that are specific not only for the hapten but also for a different carrier protein.
B cells of a secondary response can inhibit a subsequent primary response to the same antigen, provided that they are specific for a different epitope on the antigen.
the presence of hapten-specific B cells in the secondary response can prevent the synthesis of anti-hapten antibodies by B cells of the primary immune response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IgE response can be inhibited by B cells of another isotype, which may provide a new tool for studying the development of IgE antibodies.
secondary B cells can inhibit IgE responses in a hapten-specific way.
secondary B cells of different specificities can interact to regulate IgE responses.
